source.text: @all [Task Completed] Hello everyone, the task "Verify the accuracy of alarm rule creation and trigger logic" for the Enterprise Energy Consumption Monitoring and Energy Saving Diagnosis System has been completed. All test cases have passed, including various single conditions, combined conditions, and boundary value scenarios. The few issues discovered yesterday have also all been regression verified and passed. The final test report has been uploaded to Confluence. 🎉

source.speaker: Mingzhi Li
source.text: Good morning everyone. Today is Thursday. Just a reminder to @Hanqiang Liang and @Huihong Tian, your medication check-in module and family member invitation interface are due today. Please make sure to complete the delivery today. Other colleagues, please also share your plans and progress for today.

source.speaker: Lujian Gao
source.text: Hello everyone, today I'm starting a new design task: [Designing a File Storage Solution]. Considering that our system will need to store a large number of supporting documents, reports, etc. in the future, I will focus on comparing Azure Blob and AWS S3. The evaluation dimensions will include cost, API ease of use, access permission management, and the difficulty of integration with our existing technology stack. A preliminary selection recommendation report will be provided early next week.

source.speaker: Lujian Gao
source.text: Good morning everyone. Regarding the design of our file storage solution, I conducted a preliminary evaluation of Azure Blob and AWS S3 last Friday. From the perspective of cost and ecosystem integration, AWS S3 has a slight advantage, and our other projects are also on AWS. Today, I will start designing the Bucket Policy and directory structure based on S3, for example, isolating by tenant and file type.

source.speaker: Lujian Gao
source.text: Good morning everyone, regarding the file storage solution, the complete technical design document (based on AWS S3) has been uploaded to Confluence. It includes three main parts: bucket permission policies, lifecycle rules, and recommended directory structure. @Mingzhi Li Boss Li, please review it.

source.speaker: Mingzhi Li
source.text: @Lujian Gao I've finished reviewing the document on the file storage solution. The design is very comprehensive, especially the considerations for tenant data isolation and cost optimization. The proposal is approved and can be finalized.

source.speaker: Guohua Yin
source.text: @Yang Zhao Good question. Regarding the "forgot password" process, our main security consideration is to prevent "user enumeration attacks." Therefore, regardless of whether the email entered by the user exists or not, the feedback message should be consistent, such as "If this email address is registered, you will receive an email containing a password reset link," instead of directly prompting "user does not exist." Please ensure the UI copy adheres to this principle.

source.speaker: Mingzhi Li
source.text: Email received. The core requirement is that all accounts marked as `ACCOUNT_STATUS_LOCKED` must be forcibly routed to the `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1` policy for frontend interaction. @Xinjie Li @Xuexin Yin, please assess the scope of impact on the backend.

source.speaker: Guohua Yin
source.text: The newly added policy code is `ERR_POLICY_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_V1`, defined as 'Explicit Status Alert Policy'. It is mainly used for scenarios where an account is locked, requiring explicit interruption of user operations and guidance to manual channels.

source.speaker: Xinjie Li
source.text: Received. I've reviewed the document. This strategy will be handled by `ExplicitStateAlertModule`, and the parameter `halt_downstream_triggers` is set to `true`. This means that after the backend triggers this strategy, all downstream automated notifications (emails, SMS) will be halted, right?

source.speaker: Guohua Yin
source.text: @Xinjie Li Yes, your understanding is completely correct. This is to avoid sending users redundant or potentially confusing automated messages.

source.speaker: Yunqi Qian
source.text: Received, thanks a lot! The data structure looks very clear. I plan to complete the static data integration this morning to ensure the charts render correctly. In the afternoon, I'll start researching dynamic refresh solutions, initially considering WebSocket if the backend supports it. @Mingzhi Li

source.speaker: Mingzhi Li
source.text: @Yunqi Qian Great plan. WebSocket is the best solution, but our message push service isn't fully ready yet. This task can be implemented using polling for now, for example, by requesting the interface every 10 seconds. Once the WebSocket service is stable later, we can upgrade it uniformly. This way, we can avoid blocking your current task.

source.speaker: Yunqi Qian
source.text: Okay, Boss Li, understood. Then I'll use the polling solution for now, and I'll adjust the plan.
